text:
tess_acme: hey team, since 10:10 we've been getting repeated 429s and p95 spikes on our dedicated pool rwd-ded-7. App is timing out. can someone check? cc @mike_support

mike_support: looking now, can you paste a sample request id + approximate timestamps?

tess_acme: req: req_9a3f2, happened 2026-03-15T10:12:05Z. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~2.6s, lots of 429s. model: opt-2.7b-q4, batch_size=1, MIG config requested 1g.

mike_support: thx. @jordan_infra could be co-hosting noise on node-13. grabbing metrics.

jordan_infra: pulling host metrics for rwd-ded-7/node-13. seeing sustained high SM util on slice 2 and memory-bandwidth spikes. also intermittent PCIe stalls. pasting short snippet: ```
# nvidia-smi dmon (abbrev)
Time SM % Mem% Enc% Dec%  
10:11   95   65   0    0
10:12   98   70   0    0
```

lee_oncall: any autoscale events around that time?

anna_cs: customer bought dedicated but allowed fractional MIG slices — need to confirm whether other tenants can land on same host. @tess_acme are you running any overnight batches?

tess_acme: we requested 1g per allocation but we did kick off a nightly backfill job last night that was larger. didn't think it would be co-located.

jordan_infra: checking allocation table: tenant acme-42 is on slice 2. co-resident 'lab-ops' is on slice 3 running long batch jobs. I'm seeing slice-to-slice interference: L3 thrash and NVLink/PCIe bandwidth spikes that correlate with the p95 jumps. suspect cross-slice b/w thrash causing stalls in the inference runtime.

mike_support: can we safely repro by running a small bandwidth-heavy job on lab-ops slice? want to confirm causality but careful on a dedicated pool.

lee_oncall: temporary mitigation options: 1) migrate acme-42 to an isolated node, or 2) bump their autoscale/allocated slices during peak. I can trigger a live migration if customer approves.

tess_acme: :thumbsup: please move them, we prefer no noisy cohosts.

jordan_infra: will plan migration. quick checks customers can run to confirm: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/metrics?host=node-13&metric=sm_util"` and inside node: `nvidia-smi -q -d PERF` to inspect PCIe/SM activity.

mike_support: asked infra to snapshot kernel logs and audit MIG partition history for node-13. @deploy-bot: queue a dry-run eviction for tenant acme-42 on node-13.

deploy-bot: eviction job 6734 queued (dry-run). no destructive actions taken.

jordan_infra: dry-run migration looks clean, no rolling restarts required. scheduling move to node-22 (currently empty of inference tenants). ETA ~8m.

anna_cs: i've informed the customer and applied a 2-hour credit for disruption window.

tess_acme: thanks — after move can you send p95 and 429 stats for the next 30m?

mike_support: will do, tagging #support-incidents for visibility.

jordan_infra: quick post-move update: p95 returned to baseline ~110ms, 429s dropped to zero. root cause: sustained batch on adjacent slice causing PCIe and L2 cache contention which amplified KV-cache stall latency.

lee_oncall: filing incident INC-2026-041, recommending stronger placement isolation for dedicated pools and an alert to detect slice-level bandwidth thrash.

tess_acme: appreciate the quick response :heart:
